text: Harbour City’s equalizer at 45’ exemplifies a patient positional buildup characteristic of their 4-2-3-1 structure under Tomasz Rhee, featuring 17 precise short passes over 57 seconds starting deep in their own half. The progressive carries by Elias Okafor and interplay among midfielders orchestrated final-third entries without relying on wide overloads or rapid transitions, displaying control and methodical advancement. Marek Barros’s through ball exploited a seam in Seabrook Town’s 3-4-3 defensive block, breaking their wide crossing-oriented shape via incisive vertical passing rather than crossing overloads. Harbour City dominated possession (57%) with superior pass accuracy (89.9%) and field tilt (75%), enabling them to generate a high-quality chance (xG 0.125) from 12.9 meters while sustaining low PPDA (11.5) to maintain pressure and field control before scoring. This goal illustrates disciplined buildup and exploitation of defensive structural weaknesses rather than transition or pressing trigger mechanisms.
